The researchers reported that the athletes who participated in the program increased their scores, on average, by 200 points, whereas those who did not participate raised their scores, on average, by 80 points. After reading the results of the study, Jasmine, a student athlete, decided to enroll in the program. At the end of six weeks, her score had increased by 80 points. questions.question: A researcher in sports medicine is interested in comparing the amount of daily screen time between high school students who are athletes and high school students who are not athletes. A random sample of 100 high school students who are athletes and a random sample of 100 high school students who are not athletes will be selected. Each student will be asked “Do you typically have more than 3 hours of screen time each day?” Which of the following is the most appropriate test for the researcher to use to investigate whether there is a difference in the amounts of daily screen time?
questions.title: Screen Time Athletes

options.text: A two-sample z -test for a difference between population proportions
A two-sample t -test for a difference between population proportions
A two-sample z -test for a difference between population means
A two-sample t -test for a difference between population means
A chi-square goodness-of-fit test

questions.question: Researchers studying the relationship between sleep and memory obtained a sample of 28 adults to participate in an experiment. Half of the participants were randomly assigned to a full night’s sleep, and the other half were awakened every two hours throughout the night. The following day, the participants were given a list of words to memorize and recall after one hour. Researchers recorded the number of words recalled by each participant. The p -value of an appropriate statistical test was 0.29 . Which of the following is a reasonable conclusion?
questions.title: Sleep and Memory

options.text: The data provide sufficient evidence that memory is related to sleep.
The data provide sufficient evidence that memory is not related to sleep.
A cause-and-effect relationship between memory and sleep cannot be established. However, the data provide sufficient evidence that there is an association between memory and sleep.
The data do not provide convincing evidence that memory is related to sleep.
The conditions for inference must not have been satisfied.

questions.question: A recent report stated that 30 percent of smartphone users exceed their data limit in a given month. A consumer advocacy group questions the validity of the reported percent. The group obtained a random sample of 100 smartphone users and found that 40 of them exceeded their data limit in a certain month. Of the following sampling distributions, which one should be used to test the hypothesis that the proportion is different than 30 percent?
questions.title: Smartphone Data

questions.question: A college professor administered a survey to students from three different majors: engineering, nursing, and communications. The students were asked to identify how they prefer to be contacted: e-mail, telephone, or text message. The professor then used the survey data to conduct a chi-square test. Which of the following best describes the null hypothesis for the test?
questions.title: Student Contact

options.text: There is an association between major and preferred method of communication.
There is a positive association between major and preferred method of communication.
There is no association between major and preferred method of communication.
One-third of all students at the college are engineering majors, one-third are nursing majors, and one-third are communication majors.
One-third of all students at the college prefer to be contacted by e-mail, one-third prefer to be contacted by telephone, and one-third prefer to be contacted via text message.

questions.question: A random sample of students was selected at each of two high schools to investigate whether the proportions of students who drive themselves to school are different for the two schools. Of the 100 students sampled at one high school, 25 reported driving themselves to school. Of the 200 students sampled at the other high school, 62 reported driving themselves to school. Which of the following is equivalent to the p -value for a test to determine whether there is convincing statistical evidence of a difference between the proportions of students who drive themselves to school for the two schools?
questions.title: Students Driving

questions.question: A research agency surveyed 2 ,209 residents who live in one of three districts in a county: urban, suburban, or rural. The residents were asked to choose one of four categories that aligned with their opinion on how wireless infrastructure in the county should be paid for: wage tax, sales tax, property tax, or user fee. When investigating whether opinion about how the wireless infrastructure should be paid for is independent of the district in which residents live, which of the following is the correct degrees of freedom for the appropriate chi-square test?
questions.title: Wireless Infrastructure
